paragraphs.source_en: If Nobunaga, as Nobuyasu's father-in-law, could set personal feeling aside and painfully compel him to take his own life for the sake of bringing a new order to the realm, then Ieyasu too must show no weakness: he must look far ahead, consider the greater good, and handle every matter properly.

paragraphs.source_en: If Nobunaga was the Minister of the Right appointed by the sovereign, Ieyasu too was the imperially appointed Provisional Junior Captain of the Left Division of the Inner Palace Guards; he was by no means Nobunaga's vassal. paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu had considered that Nobuyasu, young and impetuous as he was, might resist him. But never had he imagined that his son would come to him in such misery, kneeling in the torrential rain.

paragraphs.source_en: “Father...” Nobuyasu continued calling to him through the downpour. “Chikayoshi has told me everything about the anguish in your heart. I understand how you suffer, Father. I understand what you cannot speak aloud.”

units.source_en: “Father...” Nobuyasu continued calling to him through the downpour. “Chikayoshi has told me everything about the anguish in your heart. I understand how you suffer, Father. I understand what you cannot speak aloud.”
units.source_zh: “父亲……”暴雨中，信康还在呼唤着他，“父亲心中的痛苦，亲吉已经全都告诉我了，我明白父亲的苦处，明白父亲的难言之隐。”

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu staggered and nearly fell. Only by catching hold of a pillar did he manage to support himself. Hot blood surged through him, and emotion swept over him like a gale. He longed to give voice to his anguish and weep aloud. Was it truly so difficult for a man to walk steadfastly along a path of his own choosing?

paragraphs.source_en: “A warrior must obey orders and remain unmoved even if Mount Tai crumbles before him. Return without harboring resentment. Since you have been ordered to repent, remain in seclusion and reflect upon your conduct until another order arrives. That is what makes a true warrior.”

paragraphs.source_en: The son who had come seeking solace from his father, convinced that his father alone understood his innocence, had seen every hope shattered by that very father. He was in despair.
